How to set up a CRM pipeline your team will actually use

A CRM only helps if the team keeps it up to date. This test post checks that the blog studio keeps formatting when an article is pasted in. It links to a page on our site, CRM implementation, and to an outside site, HubSpot.

What a good pipeline needs

Keep the list of stages short. Each stage should describe something the customer has done.

  • Clear stages that match how you really sell
  • One owner for every deal
    • A sub-point that should be flattened into the list above
  • A weekly review, with notes kept in the CRM itself

Steps to set it up

  1. List the stages a deal goes through today.
  2. Remove any stage nobody can define in one sentence.
  3. Add the stages to the CRM and assign an owner to each deal.
  4. Review the pipeline together every week.

A note on automation

Automate reminders only after the stages are stable. Changing stages later means rebuilding every automation.

Frequently asked questions

How many pipeline stages should we have?

Only as many as your team can define clearly. Fewer stages are easier to keep accurate.

Who should own the CRM?

One person should own the setup, but every salesperson owns their own deals.
